rationale: Direct peer-reviewed clinical and functional characterization of Ramond-Elliott neurodevelopmental syndrome (RAMELN, OMIM #621421) establishes that monoallelic predicted loss-of-function variants clustered in the 5' region of TRA2B cause intellectual disability/developmental delay, microcephaly, hypotonia, and early-onset seizures that frequently manifest specifically as infantile spasms. In the defining clinical cohort of 12 individuals from 11 families, infantile spasms represent a hallmark neurological finding occurring in a substantial subset of patients, distinguishing this splicing-factor disorder from non-specific epileptic encephalopathies.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 12 individuals from 11 unrelated families with monoallelic loss-of-function variants clustered in the 5' coding region of TRA2B, all affected individuals presented with intellectual disability and/or developmental delay, frequently accompanied by infantile spasms, microcephaly, and brain anomalies.

source.title: Clustered variants in the 5′ coding region of TRA2B cause a distinctive neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: All affected individuals presented intellectual disability and/or developmental delay, frequently associated with infantile spasms, microcephaly, brain anomalies, autism spectrum disorder, feeding difficulties, and short stature.

evidence.text: Ramond-Elliott neurodevelopmental syndrome is cataloged as a distinct mendelian entity characterized by global developmental delay, hypotonia, microcephaly, and seizure phenotypes predominantly presenting in infancy.

new_directions.question_text: What is the electroclinical responsiveness of TRA2B-associated infantile spasms to first-line therapies such as ACTH, high-dose oral corticosteroids, or vigabatrin compared to other genetic epileptic spasms syndromes?
new_directions.rationale: Infantile spasms in genetic neurodevelopmental syndromes often demonstrate etiology-dependent treatment response profiles; delineating this can optimize neurodevelopmental outcomes in RAMELN.

new_directions.question_text: Do pathogenic variants located downstream of the alternative translation start site in TRA2B cause an attenuated or non-epileptic phenotype, or do they escape the dominant-negative mechanism observed with 5' variants?
new_directions.rationale: Ramond et al. demonstrated that 5' variants drive pathological overexpression of the repressive Tra2β-3 isoform; determining whether 3' variants act via simple haploinsufficiency will clarify genotype-phenotype correlations regarding seizure penetrance.
